concepts.name: Clay-painted hamon design (differential clay application defining the temper line shape/aesthetic)
concepts.open_problem: The exact line where thick clay meets thin/no clay determines the hamon's artistic shape and the nioikuchi; choosing and applying the clay resist pattern to produce a specific aesthetic line is a bespoke artist judgment with no formalized predictive model. No tool predicts the resulting hamon shape from a given clay application.
concepts.has_industrial_analog: no - industrial selective hardening (induction/laser/flame) creates a hardness boundary but never paints an artistic clay-resist hamon line; the aesthetic art has no production analog
concepts.app_market_check: 'hamon design app' / 'clay tempering pattern app': none seen (only e-commerce blogs and Wikipedia explainer)
concepts.verbatim_quote: The exact line where the thick clay meets the thin clay (or no clay) is where the nioikuchi will form.

concepts.name: Yaki-ire quench-timing by steel color glow (reading blade color in a darkened forge to pick the exact quench moment)
concepts.open_problem: Smiths judge temperature purely by the blade's color glow in a darkened room, with no thermometer; identifying the precise quench instant is exceptional tacit skill where even masters lose ~1 in 4-5 blades. No vision/AI system replicates this go/no-go judgment.
concepts.has_industrial_analog: partial - industrial hardening uses precise thermocouples/pyrometers for temperature control, but that instrument-based control is a different paradigm and does not replicate the by-eye color judgment in a clay-resisted artisanal quench
concepts.app_market_check: 'quench temperature color app' / 'yaki-ire timing app': none seen
concepts.verbatim_quote: Traditional Japanese swordsmiths perform yaki-ire in a darkened forge so they can read the exact color of the heated steel, and smiths judge temperature by the blade's color glow, requiring exceptional experience to identify the precise moment for quenching.

concepts.name: Hamon attribution / school identification by temper-line appearance (nie, nioi, hataraki reading)
concepts.open_problem: Hamon patterns and internal activities (kinsuji, ashi, sunagashi) act as a swordsmith's signature enabling attribution to schools; expert connoisseurship reading these features is tacit and unautomated. No model reliably attributes a blade to a smith/school from the hamon.
concepts.has_industrial_analog: no - this is connoisseurship/authentication of bespoke art objects; industrial heat-treatment has no equivalent of attributing a part to a 'maker' by its hardness-line micro-features
concepts.app_market_check: 'hamon identification app' / 'katana attribution app': none seen (only collector blog guides)
concepts.verbatim_quote: Hamon patterns are unique to each sword and serve as a signature of the swordsmith, showcasing their skill and school of training.

concepts.name: Swordsmith tacit-knowledge transmission under endangerment (apprenticeship-bound craft skill at risk of loss)
concepts.open_problem: Survival of sword making hinges on continuity of knowledge transmitted through a 5-10+ year unpaid apprenticeship; with ~300 licensed smiths and only ~30 full-time, the tacit skill is endangered and there is no codified/captured medium for it. Capturing and transmitting this embodied knowledge is an unsolved problem.
concepts.has_industrial_analog: no - the heat-treatment industry transmits via documented standard procedures and instruments; there is no industrial analog to preserving an endangered, body-to-body apprenticeship craft of clay-tempered sword art
concepts.app_market_check: 'swordsmith training app' / 'craft skill capture app': none seen
concepts.verbatim_quote: The survival of Japanese sword making hinges on the continuity of knowledge, which is primarily facilitated through a demanding apprenticeship system.

concepts.name: Centering clay by feel (detecting centered mass via vibration/smoothness sensed through the arm)
concepts.open_problem: Potters judge centering by feeling whether the spinning mound vibrates/bumps versus feels still and smooth; it is the hardest and most important wheel skill, taking months of muscle memory. Current AI can detect wobble but cannot separate poor technique from wheel-head resonance, causing false positives.
concepts.has_industrial_analog: partial - intelligent industrial wheel machines use high-precision sensors for automatic billet central positioning, but that mechanically auto-centers a billet and does not replicate or teach the human kinesthetic centering judgment
concepts.app_market_check: 'pottery centering app': research/pilot systems and centering jigs exist (Pott'r aid, 89%-accuracy 2024 pilot) but no robust consumer feel-judgment app seen
concepts.verbatim_quote: You can tell if your clay is centered by resting your right arm on the splash pan and feeling whether the spinning mound is vibrating and bumping, or whether it feels still and smooth as it spins.

concepts.name: Judging clay plasticity / water content by feel (stiffness sensed by hand, not measured)
concepts.open_problem: Experienced potters do not measure 21% vs 23% water; they judge the needed stiffness by feel because gauge devices are distrusted. Quantifying the 'smooth = just right' tactile setpoint, and the localized inter-particle friction it reflects, is unsolved; consumer moisture meters measure bulk conductivity, not the relevant feel.
concepts.has_industrial_analog: partial - industrial ceramics uses NIR/in-line moisture analyzers (MoistTech, Finna) to control clay moisture on production lines, but these measure bulk % moisture, not the hand-felt plasticity/workability judgment used in throwing
concepts.app_market_check: 'clay plasticity app' / 'clay moisture throwing app': none seen for throwing feel (only industrial NIR sensors and a pottery-inventory tracker, ClayMate)
concepts.verbatim_quote: Although there are a variety of devices employed to gauge stiffness, the usefulness of these is often questioned by experienced people (who prefer simply judging by feel).

concepts.name: Pulling walls to uniform thickness by fingertip feel (sensing wall irregularities and modulating pressure)
concepts.open_problem: Even wall thickness is achieved by placing a finger inside to feel irregularities and varying finger pressure (more at the thick base, delicate near the rim); this real-time tactile control loop is learned by muscle memory and is not captured by any sensing/feedback system.
concepts.has_industrial_analog: yes - industrial forming (jiggering, RAM-pressing, slip-casting) produces uniform-thickness walls mechanically against molds, replacing the hand-pulling skill entirely; but it does not replicate the by-feel pulling judgment itself
concepts.app_market_check: 'wall thickness pottery app': none seen; calipers and VR caliper sims (Dojagi) exist but no live hand-feel feedback product
concepts.verbatim_quote: To achieve uniform thickness, periodically check by placing a finger on the inside to feel for irregularities, then adjust the pressure accordingly to maintain even thickness throughout.

concepts.name: Haptic/AI capture of throwing skill (modeling the tactile clay-mechanics judgment for teaching)
concepts.open_problem: Computer-vision + neural-net and sensor-fused systems attempt to predict centering success and flag uneven pressure, but no consumer-grade AI captures sufficient depth because it relies on moisture meters calibrated for soil/food that measure bulk conductivity, not localized inter-particle friction. Faithful tactile modeling remains open.
concepts.has_industrial_analog: no - this is about teaching/modeling the human throwing judgment; industrial ceramics bypasses the skill rather than modeling it, so there is no industrial analog to the skill-capture problem
concepts.app_market_check: 'pottery skill AI app': VR sims (PotteryVR, Dojagi) and AI tutorial generators (ReelMind) exist but are explicitly noted as insufficient-depth; no mature feel-faithful product
concepts.verbatim_quote: No current consumer-grade AI system captures sufficient depth, as most rely on single-point moisture meters calibrated for soil or food — devices that measure bulk electrical conductivity, not localized inter-particle friction.

notes: HONEST findings (R5, only what I actually saw across 10 WebSearches). STRONGEST WHITE SPACE (no-industrial-analog AND zero-AI): Domain A katana concepts. (1) Clay-painted hamon design and (2) yaki-ire quench-by-color-judgment both show ai_penetration=none and no true industrial analog: industrial selective hardening (induction/laser/flame, confirmed real) creates hardness boundaries but never paints an artistic clay-resist hamon nor judges quench by eye in a clay-resisted artisanal blade. Hamon attribution (connoisseurship) and endangered swordsmith knowledge transmission are also no-analog with ~none/very-low AI. IMPORTANT HONEST CAVEAT against the v2 hypothesis on Domain B: pottery is NOT zero-AI. I saw active emerging AI/research for centering and clay judgment - a 2024 12-studio pilot claiming 89% centering-success prediction via accelerometers+strain gauges, AI wheel-speed/RPM recommenders, VR haptic sims (PotteryVR, Dojagi w/ vernier calipers), and AI tutorial generators flagging off-center/uneven pressure. BUT every source explicitly states these fall short of the human tactile judgment (cannot separate technique-wobble from wheel resonance; moisture meters read bulk conductivity not inter-particle friction). So I tagged Domain B concepts ai_penetration low/very-low (research/pilot stage, no robust consumer product), NOT none. has_industrial_analog for Domain B is mixed: industrial ceramics DOES auto-center billets and form uniform walls (jiggering/RAM/slip-casting) = partial/yes for the bulk mechanical outcome, but does NOT replicate the by-feel centering/plasticity/pulling JUDGMENT (the artisanal task). Net: katana art = cleaner no-analog/no-AI white space than pottery; pottery has analog-for-bulk-process plus a thin but real layer of pilot-stage AI, so it only partly satisfies the v2 no-industrial-analog + zero-AI filter. App-market checks returned 'none seen' for every specific artisanal-judgment task (hamon design, quench timing, plasticity-by-feel, wall-thickness-by-feel); only adjacent products exist (industrial NIR sensors, centering jigs, inventory tracker, VR sims).
